observation: The client hooks that 'agent-loop init install-assets' installs resolve their runtime as '<repository-root>/vendor/autoload.php' and otherwise register '<repository-root>/src' as the PSR-4 root of voku\AgentLoop. This repository installs agent-loop as an isolated Composer tool project (tools/agent-loop), because the CLI needs PHP >= 8.3 while the library still supports PHP >= 7.1, and its own src/ is the parser library. The installed SessionStart hook therefore mis-registered the host source tree and failed with 'agent-loop Claude context hook failed: Class "voku\AgentLoop\AgentGuidance\AgentDisciplineHook" not found'.

evidence.summary: Printed 'Class voku\AgentLoop\AgentGuidance\AgentDisciplineHook not found' with the package-owned hook installed; the same command returns the discipline payload after the host-owned hook bundle resolves tools/agent-loop/vendor/autoload.php first.

hypothesis: A hook that hard-codes one autoload location cannot be installed into a repository that keeps the tool outside its root Composer project, and its fallback makes the failure worse by claiming the host's src/ as the package source root.
validated_conclusion: The package-owned hooks should resolve their runtime from an ordered candidate list that includes a host-configured path (for example an 'agent_loop_autoload' key in .agent-loop/init.json) instead of only '<root>/vendor/autoload.php', and the src/ fallback should verify that the directory actually contains the package before registering it.

validation_case.given: agent-loop is installed as an isolated Composer tool project outside the repository root
validation_case.then: the hook resolves the package runtime from the host-configured location instead of failing
